visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A young man with black hair and a teal T-shirt stands in a brightly lit indoor space. A red 'anger' emoji sticker is attached to his forehead. He moves his arms rhythmically, posing with crossed arms while text overlays appear centrally. (2) A close-up shot shows a bottle of 'Heisong' pure water. The bottle is filled to the very top, and text captions are positioned over the label. (3) The man in the teal shirt reappears, looking slightly to the side with the same angry expression and emoji. He stands in a neutral indoor hallway. (4) A close-up shows a partially opened paper drink carton from 'Uni-President'. The top is torn unevenly, and green liquid is visible inside. (5) The man returns, looking directly at the camera with his arms crossed and a serious, frustrated facial expression. (6) A shot of an urban street intersection shows a traffic light with a digital countdown display showing 91 seconds. Apartment buildings are visible in the background. (7) The man appears again in a close-up, leaning slightly forward with a focused, intense gaze. (8) A shot looking up at an outdoor wall features a 'Hitachi' air conditioning unit. Water is dripping from the unit. (9) The man concludes by looking down at the camera, then back up, maintaining his rhythmic posing.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video aims to humorously identify common daily life frustrations experienced by foreigners (specifically Japanese) living in Taiwan. It uses a rhythmic, meme-style editing format to list specific annoyances like overfilled water bottles, difficult packaging, and long traffic lights, using the creator's exaggerated frustrated reactions to create relatable comedic content.

endorsement_analysis.endorsementCues: Products are used as examples of frustration rather than being promoted.

high_inference.freeDescribe: The video follows a popular short-form trend where creators use a specific BGM track (Ira Ira) to catalog pet peeves. The combination of Japanese vocal samples and Chinese captions highlights a cross-cultural perspective.
